Shallow ReLUs Networks in $L^p$-Type and Sobolev Spaces:
Approximation and Path-Norm Controlled Generalization*
Weizhao Li
School of Mathematical Sciences
Fudan University
Shanghai, China
WEIZHAOLI24@M.FUDAN.EDU.CN
Fanghui Liu
School of Mathematical Sciences
Institute of Natural Sciences and MOE-LSC
Shanghai Jiao Tong University
Shanghai, China
FANGHUI.LIU@SJTU.EDU.CN
Lei Shi
School of Mathematical Sciences
Shanghai Key Laboratory for Contemporary Applied Mathematics
Fudan University
Shanghai, China
LEISHI@FUDAN.EDU.CN

Abstract

We study approximation by shallow ReLUs networks, $\sigma_s(t)=\max\{0,t\}^s$, and the gener-
alization behavior of such networks under $\ell_1$ path-norm control. For the $L^p$-type integral
spaces $\mathcal{F}_{p,\tau}^{s}$, $1\leq p\leq 2$, we prove approximation bounds for shallow networks using spher-
ical harmonic analysis. In particular, when the parameter measure is the uniform measure
$\tau$, and $p<p^*=\frac{2d+2}{d+3}$, we obtain the rate $O(\text{[illegible]})$, which im-
proves the corresponding random-feature rate. We also derive approximation rates for
Sobolev spaces $W^{\alpha,p}$ in the range $1\leq p<2$ by embedding them into spectral Barron
spaces. Finally, for nonparametric regression with sub-Gaussian noise, we prove minimax-
optimal generalization bounds for path-norm-regularized shallow ReLUs networks: the
rates are $O(\text{[illegible]})$ over $\mathcal{B}^{s}_{\text{[illegible]}}$, over $W^{\alpha,\infty}$, with matching
lower bounds up to logarithmic factors.

Keywords:   Neural Networks, Sobolev Spaces, Variation Spaces, Path Norm

1  Introduction

Deep learning has shown remarkable effectiveness in high-dimensional approximation prob-
lems, particularly in scientific computing, inverse problems, and operator learning (Han
et al., 2018; Adcock et al., 2022; Beck et al., 2023). In many such settings, the ReLUs
activation $\sigma_s(t)=\max\{0,t\}^s$ ($s\in\mathbb{N}_0$) is especially relevant because it yields piecewise
polynomial representations that are well suited to smooth targets and derivative-sensitive
tasks (Yang and Zhou, 2025; He et al., 2024).

*.  Authors are listed in alphabetical order and contributed equally to this work. Corresponding authors:
